item.title: Ukraine rejects permanent curbs on farm exports after joining EU, PM tells Euronews
item.description: Ukraine’s PM tells Euronews that EU limits on Ukrainian wheat and grain must be transitional, with clear exit conditions, not a permanent restriction.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 3rd, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 3rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Portugal housing protesters hail court win, but ruling limits tents to one activist
item.description: The court ruling letting Renata Cambra keep her tent in Rossio overnight is a win for the housing rights movement, but it does not recognise collective occupation of the square.

item.title: Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia postponed to December over regional security
item.description: The Asian Football Confederation cited “exceptional circumstances” and travel disruptions in moving the tournament from January 2027 to late December, after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia forced the Dakar Rally and the WTA Finals to be cancelled or relocated.

item.title: EU electoral systems: Europe cannot lead without leaders voters choose
item.description: Europe's electoral systems reward politicians for pleasing party bosses, not persuading voters write Alberto Alemanno, Professor at HEC Paris, and political analyst Samuel Dempsey in an opinion piece for Euronews. Until that changes, those best at winning public support will be the EU's opponents.

item.title: Cut down ‘outdated’ nitrate limit in drinking water, health and environmental groups tell WHO
item.description: Health and environmental groups have urged the World Health Organization (WHO) to overhaul its decades-old nitrate limit for drinking water, saying that even low levels of nitrate can be linked to cancer and premature birth.

item.title: Iran warns of ‘new battlefield’ after reported US strike on Qeshm
item.description: Parliament speaker Ghalibaf said “the ball is in America’s court to prevent war” as Iran reached its highest defensive readiness and Iranian outlets reported Tehran had updated its target bank to include US support bases in Europe under a “response without geographical limits”.

item.title: Which countries in Europe have been hit by supermarket fridge cyber incidents?
item.description: A total of nine countries have been affected by suspected cyber attacks on 2 November that turned fridges onto defrost setting, including Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, and Italy.

item.title: Who will replace Lagarde? Eurozone picks nominees as race for ECB top job begins
item.description: Eurozone countries have until Friday to put forward candidates to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank, with finance ministers due to take stock of the nominations on 9 November, a Eurogroup spokesperson told Euronews.

item.title: Lufthansa faces €2 billion extra fuel bill as Iran war keeps prices high
item.description: Germany’s Lufthansa reported higher summer profit and record quarterly revenue, but rising fuel costs prompted it to lower the upper end of its annual profit forecast.

item.title: Ranked: The world's 15 safest cities for travellers in 2027 – and nine are in Europe
item.description: European cities like Zürich, Amsterdam and Reykjavik are among the safest in the world for travellers, according to a new ranking.

item.title: US midterm elections results 2026: Live updates in maps and charts
item.description: Follow the 2026 US midterm election results live as votes are counted, with real-time updates on the races that will determine control of Congress.

item.title: Spanish footballer Jesús de Miguel dies after collision with goalkeeper, club says
item.description: De Miguel was challenging for the ball in midfield during Monday’s match when he was struck in the chest by Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during the final minutes at Estadio Heliodoro Rodríguez López.

item.title: Vivienne Jolie legally drops estranged dad Brad Pitt’s name
item.description: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt’s daughter Vivienne becomes their fourth child, after Shiloh, Maddox and Zahara, to officially drop "Pitt" from their surname.

item.title: Hungary is not blocking Ukraine's EU accession talks, Kyiv's ambassador insists
item.description: Ukraine's envoy to the EU, Taras Kachka, told Euronews that Hungary has no new substantive objections to opening the country's remaining two negotiating clusters, despite recent delays in Budapest. His remarks come a day before the European Commission's latest enlargement assessment.

item.title: Child dies in New York’s first measles-linked death in over 30 years
item.description: A child has died from a measles-associated illness in rural northern New York, marking the state’s first known measles-related death in more than three decades, health authorities have confirmed.

item.title: Russia pounds Ukraine with 289 drones and 17 ballistic missiles in overnight strikes, Zelenskyy says
item.description: In a fresh push for diplomacy as the conflict grinds through its fifth year, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said on Tuesday that Washington-led talks between Russia and Ukraine were set to resume next week.

item.title: Top destinations and most bookings: Where did Europeans travel to in 2026?
item.description: Data released by eDreams ODIGEO has revealed the online travel agency’s most-booked destinations for European travellers in 2026.

item.title: Collins English Dictionary reveals their 2026 Word of the Year: Do you know what 'Mogging' means?
item.description: A popular slang term among Gen Z and Alpha, "mogging" is currently used in a playful way – even if it has a darker backstory.

item.title: King Charles and Queen Camilla caught in heavy rain during Antigua celebrations
item.description: King Charles III and Queen Camilla were caught in a downpour while attending Antigua and Barbuda’s Independence Day celebrations at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium.

item.title: 'Gridlock will be the word of the day' if Democrats win the midterms, says Republican strategist Matt Klink
item.description: Euronews' Stefan Grobe speaks to Matt Klink, a Republican party strategist, and president of Klink Campaigns. He comments on the upcoming US midterm elections due to happen across the US today.

item.title: Montenegro to join EU by 2028 'very realistic', says Podgorica's representative
item.description: Petar Marković, Montenegro's ambassador to the EU, said his country is the "frontrunner" among the EU candidate countries.

item.title: How can the EU support 50 million Europeans who can’t heat their homes?
item.description: On October 29, EU energy ministers met in Luxembourg to address the severe winter energy affordability crisis. Driven by conflicts in the Middle East and the war in Ukraine, wholesale gas prices have surged to nearly €100 per megawatt-hour.

item.title: Rhodes floods: Cars swept away after torrential rain in Greece
item.description: Floodwaters swept vehicles and debris through Archangelos on Rhodes, damaging dozens of homes and businesses as more storms remain possible.

item.title: Police dismantle housing cost protest camp in central Madrid, city authorities say
item.description: The camp sprang up on 26 September following the police eviction of an 87-year-old pensioner from her lifelong Madrid home, after the real estate company that owned the apartment drastically raised the rent.

item.title: The race to join the EU: Who’s in pole position — and who’s falling behind?
item.description: Good morning. My name is Angela Skujins and welcome to your Tuesday newsletter. On today’s menu: The who’s who of those wanting to join the 27 member club gather for an exclusive EU Enlargement Summit hosted by Euronews. Here’s what you need to know today.

item.title: Saudi Aramco profits jump 35% despite attacks on oil facilities
item.description: Higher oil prices and a joint venture sale lifted the Saudi giant’s earnings, even as disrupted exports and prolonged conflict weighed on the kingdom’s economy.

item.title: Europe Today: Euronews Enlargement Summit kicks off in Brussels as US midterms test Trump
item.description: Brussels hosts the Euronews Enlargement Summit as Montenegro, Albania and Ukraine push for EU membership. We speak to the EU ambassadors of Montenegro, Petar Marković, and Ukraine, Taras Kachka. Plus: Republican strategist Matt Klink on how today's US midterms test Donald Trump.

item.title: North Korea slams FBI claims it was behind €5bn Binance hack and test fires missiles
item.description: A 2024 United Nations report said proceeds from North Korean cyberattacks had "reportedly helped to fund the country's development of weapons of mass destruction".

item.title: Why are supermarket freezers being hacked across Europe and could AI make it worse?
item.description: Who is responsible for the cyber attacks on supermarket freezers in Europe and why will it get worse with AI? Euronews Next spoke to cybersecurity experts for answers.

item.title: Apple earnings beat expectations, but rising chip costs worry investors
item.description: Better-than-expected results from Apple for the last quarter of the company’s fiscal year 2026 were overshadowed by rising memory chip costs and a forecast for slower services growth.

item.title: Thousands of troops from Europe to rehearse post-war Ukraine deployment in Poland
item.description: The force, which was set up in 2025 and already has an operational headquarters in Paris, is not a NATO operation and has little US involvement.

item.title: ‘The forest is an act of love’: Italy’s truffle hunters step in to save drought-hit harvests
item.description: Reforestation can help lower soil temperatures, retain moisture and reduce erosion in woodlands where climate change is shrinking truffle harvests.

item.title: Beyond five stars: 10 signs you’re staying in an ultra-luxury hotel, from house cars to turndown gifts
item.description: The five-star rating system can’t account for the personalised service offered at the very best hotels around the world.

item.title: Thailand, An Exquisite Address Beyond Travel Experiences
item.description: As work becomes borderless and global citizens rethink where they live, Thailand is emerging as a destination not only to visit, but to experience, return to and, for some, call a second home.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 3rd, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 3rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: EU enlargement at a turning point as leaders gather for Euronews summit
item.description: Leaders meet at Euronews’ second Enlargement Summit at a pivotal moment for EU expansion. Montenegro is held back by bilateral disputes, Albania by protests, while Moldova and Ukraine make uneven progress. The Commission’s roadmaps risk widening the gap between frontrunners and stalled candidates.

item.title: Human-driven climate change may have halted the onset of a new ice age, according to new study
item.description: Canadian researchers have studied changes in the vast Barnes Glacier over the last 3,000 years.

item.title: Spain introduces paid menopause sick leave from December 2026
item.description: From 1 December, female workers with impairing conditions linked to the menopause can access specific medical leave. Spain thus expands labour protection for women, while other European countries still do not provide a similar measure.

item.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island ahead of midterm elections
item.description: The strikes on Iran come on the eve of US midterm elections, and just hours after Trump signalled progress in negotiations with Tehran.

item.title: British adventurer returns home after 28-year journey around the world
item.description: British adventurer Karl Bushby returns to his mother’s home in Hull after completing a 28-year, 50,000-kilometre journey from Chile.

item.title: British government sets out tougher rules for migrants looking to settle in the UK
item.description: British PM Andy Burnham said the UK had "lost control of immigration" following Brexit. "This Home Secretary is gripping this problem, and she has my full support in doing so."

item.title: Britain’s 'oldest cars' hit the road for annual London to Brighton run
item.description: The UK celebrates 140 years of the motor car as pre-1905 vehicles parade through London's historic streets before heading to Brighton.

item.title: Ukraine says hopes of 'progress toward peace' knocked by attack on aid distribution centre
item.description: Zelenskyy said the Zaporizhzhia attack showed Russia was "sending an entirely opposite signal" and that it was "counting on more killings."

item.title: Recent virus outbreaks show urgent need to complete pandemic treaty, says WHO chief
item.description: The WHO chief said recent outbreaks of Ebola and hantavirus show why countries must finalise the agreement without delay.

item.title: Climber rescued after being abandoned at 2,600 metres in Austrian Alps
item.description: Gerhard Kremser, the district manager of the Pongau Mountain Rescue Service, said the man likely would not have survived another night on the mountain due to the conditions.

item.title: Inside Milipol Qatar, where drones and robots take on security and emergency response roles
item.description: From a drone carrying traffic lights to a remotely operated robot, exhibitors at Milipol Qatar demonstrate equipment designed for emergency response, surveillance and work in dangerous places.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 2nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Watch: Unseen images of drone sinking Greek tanker off Bulgarian coast
item.description: Russia is suspected of being behind a recent wave of attacks targeting commercial vessels in the Black Sea.

item.title: Ebola kills over 5,300 in fastest-growing outbreak on record
item.description: The outbreak, caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, has infected more than 10,000 people since May and has spread to Kenya, Uganda and Nigeria.
